lore_anchors.definition: A rare concealment formation that suppresses the emission of spiritual energy from a location, making hidden caves or treasures nearly undetectable to standard spiritual sense.

A darkly pragmatic euphemism in cultivation fiction for a decisive assassination, where the killer treats the victim's head as a token to be collected and presented for political or mercenary purposes.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Han Li kill the Green Sun Sect elder so suddenly?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He was never truly working for the sect. He was biding his time, treating the 'alliance' as a temporary cover. Killing Elder Ding was a tactical move to eliminate a witness and 'borrow' a head as a bargaining chip to negotiate with or intimidate Yuan Yao's other pursuers.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Is Han Li helping Yuan Yao because he likes her?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Not really. This follows the Mortal Stream rule of 'never lift a finger without benefit.' Han Li calculates that saving Yuan Yao will yield a future debt or a specific reward, likely related to her knowledge of the Void Heaven Palace or a powerful artifact. Saving her is a transaction, not an act of love.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why doesn't Han Li just run away from the whole situation?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Running would mean abandoning a valuable asset (Yuan Yao) to her death and losing a chance to eliminate a loose end (the Green Sun Sect witnesses who saw his face). Han Li's instinct is not to flee from a problem, but to 'eliminate the data'—silence those who can connect him to this event.
